name: temperature_pressure_effects_dissociation
title: Temperature and pressure effects on dissociation of combustion products
summary: Equilibrium dissociation of the products of octane (C8H18) combustion with 20 % excess dry air: the 14-species equilibrium mole fractions from the EES built-in Chem_Equil procedure at given pressure and temperature, the pressure/temperature trends of the exercise kept as two $IF parametric-sweep blocks.

verification.summary: EES stored point (last row of the temperature sweep, T = 3000 K, P = 10000 kPa, solved in a scratch copy): 21 common variables, 10 differ at rtol 0.001. Major species x_CO2 6.06e-04 and x_N2 3.44e-04; largest difference 9.41e-02 on x_NO2 (NASA-Glenn vs EES JANAF). The shipped file is the default point, 10 MPa and 2500 K.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of Ex_2_T&P effects on dissociation.EES (TM-0230): P = 10000 kPa, T = 3000 K and the 14 mole fractions
verification.notes: compare_solution.py --ees-units on the scratch copy at T = 2726.85 C: '21 common variables, 10 differ (rtol=0.001)'. P, T, element ratios, x_Ar and sumx agree; x_CH4 = 2.4e-14 against a stored 0 (inside atol, warning W002). x_OH 5.73e-02, x_NO 3.74e-02, x_NO2 9.41e-02: EES Chem_Equil uses older JANAF data, CoolSolve the NASA-Glenn polynomials. Shipped .sol is the default point (2226.85 C), 2 iterations.
